System: You can't join a sect yet.
About the sect

The Beggars' Sect's
twin treasures are
the Dog-Beating
Staff and the
Eighteen Dragon-
Subduing Palms. Its
brothers beg far and
wide, and from that
life came the Dog-
Beating Staff, a
superb art passed by
word of mouth from
chief to chief. Its
eight secrets -
trip, chop, wrap,
jab, flick, lead,
seal, turn - hide
subtle changes and
wondrous moves: an
art of the very
first rank. The
Eighteen Dragon-
Subduing Palms are
the hardest,
strongest palm art
under heaven;
without uncommon
palm strength and
internal energy, no
one can unleash
their full power.
Beyond staff and
palm, the sect's
fists, kicks, and
arts of poison and
antidote also excel.

System: You've wiped out the Demon Cult!

The Demon Cult's
palm arts are its
strongest, then its
finger, sword and
spear arts. The
heart of its way is
attack as defense,
so every move is
vicious and leaves
the enemy no room to
breathe; but if your
internal energy runs
dry and the assault
breaks off, the
damage you take is
hard to predict. Its
deepest art is the
Star-Absorbing Art,
a fearsome skill
that drains the
enemy's internal
energy for your own
use. It gives you an
endless flow of
energy, and once the
enemy's is spent, he
can neither strike
nor even parry: he
is left as meat on
the chopping block.

System: You've wiped out the Huashan Sect!

The Huashan Sect is
also famed for its
swordplay: light,
nimble and deft,
like a pair of
swallows dancing
among spring
willows, high and
low, left and right,
turning at will. Its
finest sword art is
the Nine Swords of
Dugu: beat slow with
fast, strike last
yet land first. If
the enemy's moves
have any pattern, it
finds their weak
points and breaks
their style. It
holds a way to break
every blade, sword,
fist, foot, spear,
staff and hidden
weapon: truly the
finest sword art
under heaven. Beyond
the sword, Huashan's
palm art is also
distinctive: driving
the palm with qi,
wide open and all-
out, it hits a huge
area.

System: You've wiped out the Hero Sect!

The Hero Sect comes
from the Western
Regions, so its arts
were once quite
unlike those of the
Central Plains
sects. But bent on
ruling the martial
world of the Central
Plains, it kept
expanding and took
in the best of every
school, until its
arts became a real
mixed bag. Its
stress on spells
comes from its
roots: many of its
leading figures were
once army generals,
so sorcery is prized
above all. Strongest
of all is the
Tornado, a mighty
spell fusing the
natural wind with
the essence of the
Central Plains'
arcane arts. Besides
that, the sect does
pretty well with
saber, sword and
fist too.

The Shenlong Gang is
a small sect of the
Changbai Mountains,
little known in the
martial world, but
medicine and
antidotes are its
specialty: win its
help, and your life
gains an extra
safeguard. One of
its past chiefs was
a man of rare
genius. He pondered
for seven years
beside the Heavenly
Lake, and from the
changes of sun and
moon he grasped a
profound art, the
Flame Dragon, which
became the gang's
treasure. But the
chiefs after him
were mediocre: the
manual was handed
down, yet no one
ever mastered it.
